summary_paragraph: A woman with chronic lymphedema, morbid obesity, and a history of recurrent cellulitis was admitted for worsening bilateral leg swelling extending into the thighs and lower back, despite recent treatment with ceftriaxone and outpatient diuretics. Imaging ruled out deep vein thrombosis, and CT of the thigh revealed varicose veins without a mass. She was treated with IV furosemide, leading to improved edema. During the hospitalization, she developed a cough and rising white blood cell count; a repeat chest X-ray showed left lower lobe pneumonia, prompting a course of levofloxacin. She also experienced an anaphylactic reaction to Lumason during an echocardiogram, which was treated promptly and added to her allergy list. Her home diuretic, bumetanide, was resumed, and she was discharged on oral antibiotics, penicillin prophylaxis, and all prior medications. She was referred to allergy and lymphedema clinics for follow-up.
problems: Anaphylactic reaction due to adverse effect of correct drug or medicament properly administered, initial encounter
Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories
Epilepsy, unspecified, not intractable, without status epilepticus
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of other female genital organs
Hypertensive heart and chronic kidney disease with heart failure and stage 1 through stage 4 chronic kidney disease, or unspecified chronic kidney disease
